beats.say: Before you write any code, draw the map.
Supplier files arrive by SFTP. Clicks pour out of the app. And orders live in MySQL.
beats.label: Cymbal's sources

beats.say: Three ideas: the shape of the pipeline, the network, and the keys.
beats.label: Station 2.1 · Planning the pipelines
beats.head: Shape. Network. Keys.

check.prompt: Why does ELT load the raw data first?
options: You can fix a bug and process the data again
check.why: The raw copy stays. So a fix or a backfill can start from it again.

beats.say: First, two words: batch and streaming.
Batch is like the post. Letters are collected, then delivered together, on a schedule.
beats.label: Batch
beats.head: Like the post: collected, then delivered

beats.say: Streaming is like a phone call. Each event is handled as it happens.
beats.label: Streaming
beats.head: Like a phone call: as it happens

beats.say: Next: ETL or ELT? It is only a question of when you transform.
beats.label: ETL or ELT
beats.head: When do you transform?

beats.say: ELT loads the raw data into BigQuery first, then transforms it with SQL. It is the default.
beats.label: The default
beats.head: ELT: load raw, then transform in SQL

beats.say: Why? The raw copy stays. So you can fix a bug, and run it all again.
beats.label: Why raw first
beats.head: Keep the raw copy. Replay any time.

beats.say: The classic streaming path: Pub/Sub, then Dataflow, then BigQuery.
beats.label: The streaming path to remember

beats.say: And for database changes: Datastream, straight into BigQuery.
beats.label: The change-capture path
beats.head: Database → Datastream → BigQuery

beats.say: The trap: devices writing straight into the database. Always buffer with Pub/Sub.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Devices writing straight to the database. Buffer with Pub/Sub.

check.prompt: Workers have no public IP and must call BigQuery. What do you turn on?
options: A public IP on one worker
check.why: Private Google Access lets private workers reach Google APIs.

beats.say: Second: the network. Workers need a way to talk.
Secure workers have no public IP address. So how do they reach Google's services?
beats.label: The puzzle
beats.head: No public IP. Now what?

beats.say: Turn on Private Google Access on the subnet. That is the private door to Google APIs.
beats.label: To reach Google APIs
beats.head: Private Google Access

beats.say: And if they need the wider internet, add Cloud NAT.
beats.label: To reach the internet
beats.head: Cloud NAT

beats.say: To reach Cloud SQL, use its private IP, or the Auth Proxy. Never open it to the whole internet.
beats.label: To reach Cloud SQL
beats.head: Private IP or the Auth Proxy

beats.say: One trap. Dataflow workers are stuck, and cannot talk to each other.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Dataflow workers cannot talk to each other.

beats.say: A firewall rule is missing, for ports 12345 and 12346.
beats.label: The fix
beats.text: Open TCP ports 12345 and 12346 between workers.

beats.say: Third: the keys.
Data moving between services is encrypted for you. Nothing to do.
beats.label: In transit
beats.head: Encrypted in transit, automatically

beats.say: For data at rest, put your own key, your CMEK, on every hop.
beats.label: At rest
beats.head: Your CMEK on every hop

beats.say: That means the Pub/Sub topic, the Dataflow job, the bucket, and the table.
beats.label: Every hop

beats.say: Recap.
Land raw data first, and transform later. Buffer streams with Pub/Sub.
beats.label: Station 2.1 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Private workers need Private Google Access. And your key goes on every hop.
beats.label: Station 2.1 · 2 of 2

beats.say: Now try the checkpoint below.
